reading.identification: A small open-sided timber-and-metal terrace canopy (OSM building=roof, 8 m2, 4.4 x 1.9 m) lean-to against the flank wall of the Vleeshuistragel passage beside the Groot Vleeshuis in Ghent, sheltering the Leie-side seating of the Groentenmarkt beer cafe — a shelter over clutter, not a house facade.
reading.notes:
TARGET IS NOT A FACADE. building=roof + 8 m2 + attached_neighbours=1 = open-sided lean-to canopy over a cafe terrace. Treat as a roof plate on posts, open on all free sides.

HEIGHT: do not use height_m 9.0 — height_source is "no-data", it is a default fallback. A terrace canopy here is ~2.4 m at the eaves, ~3.0 m at the high side against the party wall. I set ground_height_m 3.0 as the true overall structure height; upper_height_m 2.2 is schema-mandated filler and is unused (count=1).

SET A IS UNUSABLE FOR THIS TARGET. The magenta box in the plate is the bogus 9 m height projected onto the quayside row behind; it outlines a different, taller building. Nothing in set A was read as evidence. Inhouse 3D tiles cannot resolve an 8 m2 canopy in any case.

WINDOW RECORD IS A NULL PLACEHOLDER. There is no glazing and no wall to glaze. width/height/reveal/glazing_bars are schema-minimum filler — emit zero window instances. bays=1 is likewise degenerate: one open bay between corner posts.

GROUND FLOOR = arcade, chosen for physics not style: the ground level is open air between posts, with partial dark windbreak screens on the alley side (seen, photo 0). I deliberately did not choose cafe_glazing — that would place a specular glass panel where a 28 GHz ray should pass through.

LEDGES: cornice=true denotes a projecting eaves fascia + gutter beam ~0.15 m deep along the low edge, i.e. a real diffracting wedge on the silhouette, NOT a moulded classical cornice. No sills, string courses or balconies exist. Marked inferred: the red fascia and galvanised swan-neck downpipe clearly visible in photo 0 belong to the ADJACENT passage wall, not to the target.

MATERIAL: dark-stained sawn timber boarding for the deck, screens and posts; metal for the frame, gutter and fixings. roughness 2.5 mm RMS carries the board shadow-gaps in the 1-10 cm regime. Marked inferred — the canopy fabric is occluded by the OMER parasol (photo 1) and by the tree (photo 0). The red English-bond brick prominent in photo 0 is the neighbouring wall and must NOT be applied to this footprint.

ROOF: shed, high edge against the attached party wall, draining outward toward the quay; ridge/high edge parallel to the 4.4 m frontage along the path. Inferred — set B is weak for roof form and this one is fully occluded. Flat is the plausible alternative if the generator prefers it; both read the same at street level.

CLUTTER IS THE REAL CONTENT HERE (seen, both photos): black bistro tables and stacking chairs under and beside the canopy, one or more large dark parasols (~2.5 m, taller than the canopy itself and the dominant scatterer), dark vertical windbreak screens, a steel quay railing, and the Leie water surface immediately beyond. Populate these. Do NOT place vehicles — car_access is none on Vleeshuistragel and the surface is gravel; this is the exact failure that filled a pedestrian square with parked cars.

DETAIL BUDGET: 3.1 m from the path, so this is close-in — spend on the fascia edge, the post line, the terrace furniture and the railing. Nothing else on this object deserves geometry.
